newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cartel probe adds to Lufthansa's woes.
newsitem.headline: Cartel probe adds to Lufthansa's woes.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG on Monday confirmed a cartel office probe into its pricing structure, news which comes hard on the heels of Lufthansa's disappointing first half 1996 figures.

The airline said last Monday that first-half 1996 pre-tax profits fell 37 percent to 119 million marks amid price slashing by the group's European rivals, but said full-year earnings should be stable.
"It's difficult to see Lufthansa having a stable year for earnings," said Robert Willis, German analyst at Schroder Securities in London.

Lufthansa was hit in the first half of the year by disappointing growth in passenger and freight volumes, combined with a flood of cheap flights from subsidised airlines, excess capacity and the April fire at Duesseldorf airport.
"The company will have suffered from the Duesseldorf fire and some routes with good profits are being picked off by smaller cheaper airlines," said Willis.
Willis said the Channel Tunnel was taking some of Lufthansa's business and high-speed trains also posed a threat to the German.
Against this background, Lufthansa can hardly have wanted the week to start with news of a cartel office investigation into its pricing structure.

The German broadsheet Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung reported on Monday that Lufthansa's Frankfurt-Berlin route, costing 800 marks in business class, had prompted cartel authorities to ask the airline to disclose its pricing structure after "various complaints."
A Lufthansa spokesman said: "I can confirm that the investigation is taking place. We cannot commennt further on a running procedure."
The broadsheet said Lufthansa's business class travel between Cologne or Duesseldorf to Berlin, routes also flown by a unit of British Airways, cost only 640 marks.
Lufthansa's spokesman added: "We cannot operate without covering our costs. Noboday can force any company to set prices that do not cover costs."
The news of the probe drove the share price lower and Lufthansa closed floor trade at 208.30 marks, down 2.20 marks. The share recovered over the day to end electronic trade slightly ahead.
